body:
I am seeing this as well on MacOS but instead of falling back to a different tool it retries over and over.

I am using OpenRouter and qwen/qwq-32b:free but see similar behavior on other models as well.

I'm guessing this is a model specific issue, I've had it before when using models that might have funky tokenizers. Can you provide the model and check the search part of the diff edit to see where it differed from the actual file? I suspect it's something like confusing ' for ' or something similar.

This happens to me with sonnet3.7 very often when ACT is trying to edit large/long files (React .ts files with 1000+ lines). It often screws up at half the file and truncates, leaving to API-call waste and having me to restore manually. Very annoying.

QWQ32B LiteLLM 

So many 
Diff Edit Mismatch
The model used search patterns that don't match anything in the file. Retrying...

file.dart

<<<<<<< SEARCH

anyone knows if the issure closed?

Facing the same issue with sonnet 3.7
We have updated some of our diff edit logic. Can you update and try with the latest to see if the problem persists.
Exact same problem here, Cline can´t make any changes anymore because it consistently fails to edit files with both replace_in_file and write_to_file, even with Cline up to date.

Indeed having same issue with cline 3.9.2 and openrouter with Gemini 2.5 Pro experimental model with a python script that is 5200+ lines and 256K characters in size

Interesting, I switched to Openrouter Quasar Alpha LLM and it managed to make the changes and even took note of my prompt which says:

> You have a history of having diff edit mismatch issues - replace_in_file command failed due to a mismatch. This can happen if the file content changed slightly or if the SEARCH block wasn't precise enough., so take this into account when making the proposed changes.

The Quasar Alpha LLM model took this into account and changed the way it matched for the code! It responded in ACT mode with:

> Because the script is very large, and to avoid diff mismatch issues, I will:
> 
> First, search for the argparse parser definition to locate where to add the new flags.
> Then, add the import statement near the other imports.
> Then, add the mutually exclusive group logic.
> Then, add the conditional logic in the main function.
> I will start by searching for the argparse parser definition to identify the exact place to add the new flags.

Gemini 2.5 Pro didn't really observe my prompt note like Quasar Alpha did
I just started using Roo Code (also inside VS Code) and it doesn´t have this issue.

This seems especially problematic with Claude 4.0. I am not sure what everyone else's experience is, but 30-40% of the time I seem to get this error now, costing quite a lot of money.

> This seems especially problematic with Claude 4.0. I am not sure what everyone else's experience is, but 30-40% of the time I seem to get this error now, costing quite a lot of money.

Indeed, Claude 4.0 has issues when reading more than 900 lines of code. It tries to add more lines, but breaks down. Many lines disappear, and it reverts back to only a few lines remaining.

I have been coding using Claude 4.0 and gpt-4.1 doesn't appear to make any difference which model you select you constantly get Diff Edit Mismatch, one after the other, costing valuable api requests. Its such a frustrating experience that I've decided to ditch Cline and look for a better alternative.

This started happening to me this weekend after a Cline update. It's super frustrating and grinds development to a halt. Every change meets with "Diff Edit Mismatch" using Claude Sonnet 4, with Cline v3.17.8 this only started happening in the past week or so. Could it be due to a VSCode change?
This happens a lot to me. It isn't very pleasant. Using Claude 4 on Windows 11
Suspect this is a dupe of https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/3771
Thanks for reporting! This has been consolidated into #4384.
